Both records have `is_test=false` and `is_mock=false` according to their `context_flags`. However, the file paths tell a different story: both files live under `Tests/` directories (`WallpaperTests/AdaptiveQualityControllerTests.swift` and `CachingTests/CacheCoordinatorTests.swift`). These are clearly test files by location and naming convention, even though the pipeline did not set `is_test=true`. The decision rules say to apply "test-fixture" when `is_test=true` on any record — the flags as given do not technically trigger the restraint rule.

That said, the structural evidence is thin (`shared_field_count: 2`, no differing slots, no Jaccard score, both are `type-alias-object` with empty `fields_or_signature`). These are type aliases in separate test targets (`Wallpaper` and `Caching`) that happen to alias something clock-related. Lifting them into shared production code would couple test infrastructure across unrelated packages. The coincidental-shape signal dominates here.
